title: Cross-platform play: in or out of this multiplayer increment?
summary: The Definition is deliberately held neutral on whether the two players may sit on different platforms (e.g., one in a browser, one native desktop). Either answer composes with the current scope; what changes is validation cost and transport emphasis. Including it adds real mixed-platform requirements, device/matrix testing, and possibly a different transport priority. Excluding it keeps both players on one platform class and simplifies validation, while the platform-neutral WebSocket seam remains cheap insurance for a later increment. This is the last open scope boundary (readiness dimension 2): the increment's scope cannot be finalized until F2 is answered either way.

options.label: Include — full cross-platform support
options.description: Cross-platform play becomes a requirement: at least one browser client and one native desktop client can share one session. The Definition drops the holding platform-neutral must_not in favor of explicit cross-platform requirements and adds a mixed-platform pairing to the acceptance criteria; validation grows device/matrix coverage. WebSocket remains the transport — cross-platform reach reinforces rather than changes that choice.

options.label: Include minimally — one mixed-platform pairing, no device matrix
options.description: A bounded middle path: one mixed-platform pairing (e.g., one browser + one native client) is verified through the existing acceptance scenarios, with no formal device matrix or per-platform performance runs; breadth is explicitly deferred to a follow-up increment. F2 is decided 'in, minimally': the Definition gains a single mixed-platform acceptance criterion rather than full platform requirements.

options.label: Exclude — cross-platform is a non-goal this increment
options.description: Cross-platform is recorded as a deliberate non-goal for this increment: both players run the same platform class (e.g., two desktop clients), the holding must_not is removed, and no cross-platform requirements or acceptance are added. The platform-neutral transport seam stays as cheap insurance for a later increment, but nothing here validates mixed-platform sessions.
